title: Regular-functorial ordinary resolution of quasi-excellent rational schemes
statement: On the category of reduced Noetherian quasi-excellent schemes over $\mathbf Q$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme], [pqf-def-locnoeth], [def-exc-excellent-ring], including finite disjoint unions, there exists one ordinary desingularization rule $F$. For every input $X$ it assigns a finite tower $X_n\to\cdots\to X_0=X$ of ordinary blowups [def-nagata-global-blowup] with coherent ideal centers $I_i\subset\mathcal O_{X_i}$. Each $V(I_i)$ is nonempty, nowhere dense and regular, and $X_n$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. For every regular morphism $f:Y\to X$ between inputs, meaning flat with geometrically regular fibres, $F(Y)$ is the contraction of the scheme-theoretic pullback $f^*F(X)$ obtained by deleting exactly the unit-ideal centers. The comparisons retain all other extended ideal sheaves in their original order, respect identities and composition, and delete no stage when $f$ is surjective. The empty input has the tower of length zero. Noetherian schemes here admit finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings; quasi-excellence for schemes means quasi-excellence of their affine coordinate rings. Coherent modules and flatness are as in [pqf-def-coherent] and [def-weil-flat-morphism].

source.place: VIII Theorem 2.3.10, with 2.3.1, 2.3.4 and Remark 2.3.5, printed pp.91--93; this is the ordinary, not normalized, algorithm No Stacks tag states this combined result; the cited place is in the archived ILO volume.

proof.text: Choose once the rule $H$ for small-singular-locus pairs supplied by [lem-per-small-singular-locus-resolution]. Apply [lem-per-codimension-resolution-improvement]: start with its length-zero rule $R_0$, and recursively take the prescribed successor of the prefix $R_0,\ldots,R_d$. Successors retain the earlier rules, so this defines one sequence of rules on the entire category, including all finite disjoint unions. Write $T_d(X)$ for the closed unresolved sets. The input is reduced and Noetherian and quasi-excellent over $\mathbf Q$, precisely the category of these two cited statements. In particular $T_e(X)\subseteq T_d(X)$ for $e\ge d$ and $T_d(X)\cap X^{\le d}=\varnothing$.

Fix $X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], the nonempty family $\{T_d(X):d\ge0\}$ has a minimal member $T_N(X)$. Since the sets decrease, $T_e(X)=T_N(X)$ for every $e\ge N$. If this set contained $x$, take an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A$ from the Noetherian cover and its prime $\mathfrak p$ corresponding to $x$. By [lem-trf-noetherian-prime-finite-height] there is a finite bound $h$ on lengths of prime chains ending at $\mathfrak p$. Primes of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ are precisely primes of $A$ contained in $\mathfrak p$ with the same inclusions, so $c_X(x)\le h$. Taking $e\ge\max(N,h)$ contradicts $x\in T_e(X)$ and $T_e(X)\cap X^{\le e}=\varnothing$. Hence $T_N(X)=\varnothing$. This uses pointwise finite height, not finite dimension of $X$.

source.place: Lemma 4.1.3(ii), printed pp.27--28; finite-height detail made explicit (Stacks Tag 0BBZ)

proof.text: For every $e\ge N$, the compatibility in [lem-per-codimension-resolution-improvement], restricted to $X\setminus T_N(X)=X$, identifies $R_e(X)$ and $R_N(X)$ with ordered centers: there are no empty stages in either tower to remove. Define $F(X)$ to be this eventual constant tower (equivalently take the first index at which $T_N(X)$ is empty). The definition of the unresolved set now gives regularity of the last scheme and of every center. Coherence, nonemptiness, nowhere density, finiteness and ordinary blowups are supplied by the same lemma. For $X=\varnothing$, $R_0(X)$ already has empty unresolved set and length zero. Thus the definition gives the required empty-input convention.

Let $f:Y\to X$ be regular. Take $d$ at least the two stabilization indices of $X$ and $Y$. At this one common index [lem-per-codimension-resolution-improvement] gives $F(Y)=R_d(Y)=(f^*R_d(X))^c=(f^*F(X))^c$, including the ideals and their order. Since $f$ is flat, the pullback is an ordinary scheme-theoretic blowup tower: the level maps remain flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], so apply [thm-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change] successively at each cartesian level. An empty closed center has unit ideal, and conversely; blowing up the unit ideal is an isomorphism by [cor-nagata-blowup-cartier-iso], since the unit ideal is invertible. Thus precisely the unit-center stages are removed, even if a retained nonempty Cartier center also induces an isomorphism.

The comparisons respect composition as follows. For $Z\xrightarrow gY\xrightarrow fX$, the ideal at an original stage pulls back first to $I\mathcal O_{Y_i}$ and then to $I\mathcal O_{Z_i}$, which is its direct extension along $fg$. A unit ideal remains unit after extension. Deleting those unit stages after the first pullback and then deleting newly unit stages therefore retains exactly the same original ordered indices as direct pullback to $Z$. At retained stages the maps are the canonical flat base-change maps [def-nagata-blowup-flat-base-change-map]: on affine blowup charts they send each coefficient and each fraction $a/b$ to its image, so the maps for a composite agree with the composites on all chart generators. The chart maps glue to the same comparison, and the identity sends those generators to themselves. This proves both composition and identity compatibility, retaining the actual extended ideals.

source.place: VIII §§2.1.9,2.3.4, printed pp.88,91--92; explicit chart and ordered-index verification

proof.text: If $f$ is surjective, each map $Y_i=X_i\times_XY\to X_i$ in the uncontracted pullback is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Apply the same statement to the nonempty closed center $V(I_i)\to X_i$: its inverse image is nonempty. Its extended ideal cannot be unit, so no index is deleted. This proves the surjective clause for the same rule $F$.

tool_uses.why: Generic Noetherian minimal-closed-set principle for termination; this unit has no such topology result.
Pointwise finite height of primes, needed without a finite dimension hypothesis; generic commutative algebra.
Ordinary blowup flat base-change isomorphism, not a Fourier/perverse result.
Unit-ideal blowup is the identity since the unit ideal is invertible.
The concrete coefficientwise map proves identity/composition of comparisons.
Surjective maps stay surjective at every pulled-back level and center.
Keeps each uncontracted level map flat to apply ordinary blowup flat base change recursively.
